title: Local end-to-end verification and one manual YouTube broadcast
description:
The owner requirement: prove the fix locally without deploying, then confirm once against real YouTube ingest.

Local (Mac, VideoToolbox hardware encode):
- Run S1, S2, S4, S5 with the new pipeline and all toggles at their winning values.
- Produce a before/after table with --compare against the t3 baselines: M1, M2 breakdown, M4, Q1-Q7, wire bytes per second, enc.mode.
- Play the archive and the FLV locally; check the first 10 s and a middle 10 s for frame timing and A/V sync by eye as well as by oracle.
- Attach the report to the epic.

Box (only if available without a deploy - docker compose run --rm with the GPU overlay):
- Same S2/S5 run, plus nvidia-smi dmon showing encoder and decoder percentages, and chrome://gpu video_encode/video_decode = Hardware accelerated.

Manual YouTube gate (S6) with the owner:
- One 5 minute broadcast to a real stream key, then read the YouTube Live dashboard: dropped frames, bitrate, resolution, and the recorded playback speed. Watch it back.
- Record the dashboard numbers on the epic.

This bead is the checkpoint where the owner confirms the fix works before the density work (P3) starts.
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S4, S5, S6.
METRIC: everything.
GATE: all Q gates pass locally; S6 YouTube dashboard shows zero dropped frames and normal playback speed; the owner signs off.
PROOF: the attached before/after report and the YouTube dashboard screenshot/numbers.
NOTES: this is a verification bead - it should produce data and at most tiny fixes, not new features.
acceptance_criteria:
- Before/after table attached to the epic with M1, M2, M4, Q1-Q7 and wire rate.
- Archive and FLV play correctly locally (spot-checked by a human, not only by ffprobe).
- One YouTube broadcast completed with zero dropped frames and correct playback speed.
- Owner sign-off recorded on the epic.

title: Gateway: compressed sink -> ffmpeg -c:v copy -> tee(archive + live RTMP)
description:
Node side of t12. With a compressed, timestamped stream from the page, ffmpeg stops being a transcoder and becomes a muxer: no swscale, no rawvideo, no guessed frame rate.

compositor/src/recordings/recording.gateway.ts:
- New sink branch for the compressed format (codec=mp4 or codec=webm): spawn ffmpeg on connect (not on the first frame - the container header carries the codec parameters, and waiting for a frame is what made the raw path guess pix_fmt).
- Args: -f mp4 (or webm) -i pipe:0 with -probesize/-analyzeduration tuned low for fast startup, -map 0:v -map 0:a, archive output -c:v copy -c:a copy -f webm <room>-<stamp>.webm (H.264 + Opus in Matroska is what the current archive already is, so S3 content type, the .webm purge sweep and the upload/rename logic all keep working).
- Live output: -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 192k -ar 48000 -ac 2 -f flv, one destination, or -f tee with onfail=ignore + use_fifo for several, as today. Opus -> AAC is the only transcode and it is a fraction of a percent of a core.
- Backpressure policy: a write returning false must be counted and alarmed, and if it persists the session must be failed loudly (session log + health) rather than allowed to stretch time. The raw path silently stretched; the compressed path cannot stretch because timestamps come from the encoder, but a stalled sink still means a broken broadcast, so it must be visible.
- Keep the ingress window stats (bytes, chunks, kbps) - they are now a sanity check on bitrate rather than a firehose measure.
- Keep guardFfmpegPipes and attachFfmpegLogging exactly as they are (they fixed a process-killing EPIPE).

Also align shared/stream-quality so the copy path cannot emit a stream outside YouTube guidance (t6 sets the bitrates; this bead must not re-inflate them).
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S5.
METRIC: Q1-Q7, M2 cpu.ffmpeg_pct, drop.backpressure.
GATE: Q1 0.99-1.01, Q6 0.98-1.02, Q5 zero, Q7 conformance (H.264 High 1080p30, 3-6 Mbps, AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo 128-256k, GOP <= 2 s); ffmpeg CPU under 10 percent of a core per room.
TOGGLE: follows COMPOSITOR_ENCODE from t12.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S5 --compare=<previous>; ffprobe both the archive and the FLV; play 30 s of each.
acceptance_criteria:
- ffmpeg runs -c:v copy for both archive and live; only audio is transcoded for RTMP.
- Archive stays .webm (H.264 + Opus) so upload, purge and S3 content type are untouched.
- Q1-Q7 pass in S2 and S5 locally.
- Persistent sink backpressure fails the session loudly instead of degrading silently.
- Unit tests cover the new arg builder (extend src/recordings/rtmp.spec.ts).

title: Recorder page: WebCodecs hardware H.264 encode + Opus + fragmented MP4
description:
This is the bead that moves the media path onto the GPU. Today the page reads every composited frame back to system memory (frame.copyTo), copies it a second time (bytesToArrayBuffer) and pushes 1.6-4 Gbps through a WebSocket. Instead: hand the VideoFrame to a VideoEncoder and let the platform encoder keep it on the GPU. Only ~750 KB/s of compressed H.264 ever crosses to Node.

New file compositor/page/src/encode-pipe.ts (replacing nvenc-pipe.ts):
- MediaStreamTrackProcessor over the canvas capture track (already in use) -> VideoFrame, passed straight to encoder.encode(frame) with NO copyTo. Close the frame after encode.
- VideoEncoder config: codec avc1.640028 (H.264 High L4.0), width/height from the profile, framerate 30 (from t6), bitrate 6 Mbps, hardwareAcceleration prefer-hardware, avc format avcc (length-prefixed, what a muxer wants), latencyMode realtime. Force a key frame every 2 s (frame count % 60 == 0) to match the YouTube GOP guidance. Handle the decoderConfig event to get the avcC description for the muxer.
- Backpressure: watch encodeQueueSize; when it exceeds a small threshold (e.g. 4) drop the OLDEST non-key frame and count it, and request a key frame on recovery. Never let the queue grow unbounded - that is what produced the 33 MB socket queue and the slow-motion output.
- AudioEncoder: Opus 48 kHz stereo 192 kbps from the mixed track (MediaStreamTrackProcessor over the audio track).
- Muxer: mp4-muxer (Vanilagy, MIT, no dependencies, TypeScript, well tested) in fragmented mode so the file is streamable from a pipe; push each muxer flush to the WebSocket as it is produced. If fragmented MP4 turns out to be awkward for ffmpeg to demux from a pipe, fall back to webm-muxer by the same author (the MediaRecorder WebM path is already proven to demux from a pipe in this codebase) - decide and record the choice here.
- Wire framing: the sink needs to know this is the new format, so use codec=mp4 (or codec=webm) on the /ws/recording query, which t13 handles.
- On encoder error or unsupported config: surface it to the service (page console + a global) so go-live can refuse per t14 instead of silently producing nothing.

Keep MediaRecorder available behind COMPOSITOR_ENCODE=mediarecorder until t15 deletes it, so the A/B is possible.
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S5.
METRIC: C1 enc.mode, C2 enc.hw_api, M1, M2, wire bytes per second, Q1-Q7, G1 (box).
GATE: enc.mode=hw (videotoolbox locally, vaapi on the box); wire rate ~750 KB/s not 199 MB/s; M1 down >= 70 percent versus the baseline; Q1 0.99-1.01, Q2 >= 0.97 x fps, Q3 <= 8 ms, Q5 zero drops, Q6 speed 0.98-1.02.
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_ENCODE=webcodecs|mediarecorder|raw.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 --compare=bench/out/baseline-S2.json with each encode mode, and read the delta table. On the box also nvidia-smi dmon -s u during the run.
RISK: mp4-muxer fragmented + ffmpeg pipe demuxing (mitigate with the webm-muxer fallback); Chrome version differences in WebCodecs config support (log the Chromium version, assert isConfigSupported before configure).
acceptance_criteria:
- The page encodes H.264 High on the hardware encoder locally (videotoolbox) and on the box (vaapi per t5).
- No frame.copyTo / raw pixel path is used for the primary encode.
- Key frames every 2 s; bitrate and profile come from the stream-quality profile, not hard-coded.
- Encode queue backpressure drops the oldest frames with a counter instead of growing.
- Wire rate measured at roughly the configured video bitrate.
- Muxer choice (mp4-muxer vs webm-muxer) decided, justified and recorded on the epic.

title: SPIKE: can Chromium hardware-encode and hardware-decode H.264 on the T4 (VAAPI + nvidia-vaapi-driver)?
description:
DECISION GATE for the whole epic. Chromium has no NVENC backend; on Linux its only hardware video path is VAAPI, so NVIDIA needs the nvidia-vaapi-driver shim (apt package, provides /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/dri/nvidia_drv_video.so, backed by libnvcuvid and libnvidia-encode which NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=video already exposes).

Do, in a throwaway container on the g4dn.xlarge (no deploy, docker compose run):
1. apt-get install -y nvidia-vaapi-driver vainfo; export LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia, LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/dri, NVD_BACKEND=direct.
2. vainfo: list the supported VAProfile/VAEntrypoint pairs. Record whether VAProfileH264High + VAEntrypointEncSlice (encode) and VAProfileH264High + VAEntrypointVLD (decode) are present.
3. Launch the production Chromium flags plus the VAAPI feature flags and read chrome://gpu: video_encode and video_decode must say Hardware accelerated.
4. Run the t4 trial encode: confirm enc.hw_api=vaapi, watch nvidia-smi encoder percentage rise, and measure CPU for a 60 s 1080p30 encode versus the same run forced to software (prefer-software).
5. Same for decode: play/decode a 1080p30 H.264 stream and watch nvidia-smi decoder percentage.
6. Note the exact Chromium version and flag names that worked (VaapiVideoEncoder / VaapiVideoDecodeLinuxGL naming has changed across releases).

OUTCOME A (encode+decode work): proceed with t12/t13, delete the raw path (t15).
OUTCOME B (decode works, encode does not): keep a CORRECTED raw fallback for the final encode only - per-frame pts with -vsync vfr, NV12 pinned, single copy, 1080p30 - and re-scope t15 accordingly. Record this in the epic before starting t12.
OUTCOME C (neither works): escalate to the owner with options (different instance family with Intel/AMD GPU where Chrome VAAPI is first class, or accept a corrected raw+NVENC path).

Write the result as a bd decision issue or bd note on the epic, including the exact working env, flags and package versions.
design:
SCENARIO: none (throwaway container + npm run probe:gpu).
METRIC: C1, C2, C3, G1, G2, plus CPU-seconds for a fixed 60 s encode.
GATE: a written, reproducible verdict with commands and outputs.
PROOF: the spike report is attached to the epic and the owner has chosen outcome A, B or C.
NOTES: budget half a day. Do not touch the deployed stack; use docker compose run --rm.
acceptance_criteria:
- vainfo output recorded (encode and decode entrypoints).
- chrome://gpu video_encode and video_decode values recorded.
- nvidia-smi encoder and decoder percentages observed non-zero (or explicitly not).
- CPU cost of a 60 s 1080p30 encode measured for hardware vs software.
- Exact package versions, env vars and Chrome flags written down.
- Outcome A, B or C chosen and recorded on the epic before t12 starts.

title: Encoder/decoder capability probe: boot-time trial encode, health and verify script
description:
Make hardware capability an asserted fact instead of an assumption. Today the compositor discovers at go-live time (or never) that it is software-encoding.

- Add a boot-time WebCodecs trial in a throwaway page: VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported for avc1.640028 (H.264 High L4.0) with hardwareAcceleration prefer-hardware, then an actual 30-frame encode of a test pattern, confirming the encoder drains and produces output. Same idea as the existing detectNvenc trial encode, but for the encoder we actually intend to use.
- Report enc.mode (hw|sw), enc.hw_api (videotoolbox|vaapi|none), dec.mode, plus the existing renderer/compositing, in BrowserPoolService.gpuStatus() and therefore /internal/health.
- Extend probeGpuFeatureStatus reporting to include video_encode (it already collects it, only video_decode is logged) and assert on it the way assertHardwareGpuCompositing does.
- Add section 10 to scripts/verify-compositor-gpu.sh: hardware video encode and decode verdicts, and nvidia-smi encoder/decoder percentages.
- Add the same trial to src/browser/probe-local-gpu.ts so it runs locally via npm run probe:gpu.
- Log the Chromium version at boot (capability is version-dependent).
design:
SCENARIO: S1 (plus npm run probe:gpu and the verify script).
METRIC: C1 enc.mode, C2 enc.hw_api, C3 dec.mode.
GATE: locally C2=videotoolbox; on the box C2 is vaapi or none (the spike bead decides what to do about none).
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_ENCODE_PROBE=1|0 to skip the trial when it is in the way.
PROOF: npm run probe:gpu prints the encode verdict; /internal/health shows enc.mode and enc.hw_api; verify script section 10 passes locally.
acceptance_criteria:
- /internal/health reports enc.mode, enc.hw_api, dec.mode and the Chromium version.
- npm run probe:gpu prints a hardware-encode verdict without starting the service.
- verify-compositor-gpu.sh section 10 exists and is exercised on the Mac and on the box.
- Unit tests cover the verdict parsing (extend src/browser/gpu.spec.ts).

title: Baseline measurement and root-cause memo on current code (Mac + T4)
description:
Freeze the starting numbers before changing anything, so every later bead reports a real delta instead of a vibe.

- Run S1, S2, S4, S5 on main (current code, encode=raw path locally means videotoolbox, on the box it means whatever detectNvenc decided) and store the reports as bench/out/baseline-*.json.
- On the g4dn.xlarge, additionally capture: nvidia-smi dmon during S2, chrome://gpu featureStatus (video_encode, video_decode, gpu_compositing, 2d_canvas), the Chromium version, the ffmpeg build and NVENC API version, and /internal/health.
- Write the root-cause memo into the epic notes with bd note: the three causes (no timestamps on the raw wire, 1.6-4 Gbps of copies plus swscale, consume-everything VP8 software decode) each tied to a measured number.
- Set the per-bead target deltas that later beads are graded against (for example M1 baseline, and the expected drop from 60 to 30 fps).

Deliverable is data, not code. Nothing ships in this bead except bench/out baselines committed to the repo (they are small JSON).
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S4, S5.
METRIC: everything - this bead defines the reference values.
GATE: n/a (measurement only).
PROOF: bench/out/baseline-S2.json exists and its M1 value is quoted in the epic notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Baseline reports committed for S1, S2, S4, S5 on the Mac.
- Baseline report for S2 on the T4 box, including nvidia-smi and chrome://gpu snapshots.
- Root-cause memo attached to the epic with one measured number per cause.
- The owner has seen the baseline M1 and agreed the <=48 core_s target.
notes: When capturing the baseline, record how many of the 15 joined peers are ACTUALLY being decoded (streaming-cpg says late-joining producers can be silently dropped). A baseline measured with lost producers understates the real load, and the target of <=48 core_s per room-minute assumes all 10 on-scene streams are really being decoded.

title: Bench harness: CPU accounting, ffprobe quality oracle, gates and --compare
description:
The measurement half of the harness. Without it every claim in this epic is an opinion.

- CPU/memory accounting at 1 Hz over the compositor process tree: the Nest node process, every Chromium process (browser, gpu-process, renderer per tab, utility), and ffmpeg. Attribute by process tree (ppid walk) so a room can be priced. On macOS use ps -o pid,ppid,pcpu,rss,comm; on Linux read /proc/<pid>/stat utime+stime (percent-CPU from ps is a lifetime average on Linux and will lie).
- Also read CDP Performance.getMetrics from the recorder page (TaskDuration, ScriptDuration, LayoutDuration, RecalcStyleDuration) for the renderer breakdown.
- Quality oracle: after stop, run ffprobe over the archive and the live FLV and compute Q1-Q7 from the epic design (duration ratio vs the wall clock the harness measured, effective fps, frame-interval jitter p95, audio/video drift, drop and backpressure counts scraped from the session log, ffmpeg speed, codec/profile/bitrate/GOP conformance).
- Report: bench/out/<ts>/report.json plus a human report.md table.
- Gates: a per-scenario thresholds file; exit non-zero when any gate fails so CI can use it.
- --compare=<baseline.json>: print a delta table (metric, baseline, now, pct, gate) - this is the mechanism that makes each optimization individually provable.
design:
SCENARIO: all.
TOGGLE: n/a.
PROOF: run S1 twice on unchanged code; the two reports must agree within 10 percent on M1 and pass Q1-Q7. Then run --compare and confirm the delta table renders.
NOTES: M1 must be CPU-seconds, not percent-of-machine, so numbers are comparable between the 14-core Mac and the 4-vCPU T4.
acceptance_criteria:
- report.json contains every metric named in the epic design (M1-M4, Q1-Q7, C1-C3; G1-G3 when nvidia-smi exists).
- Repeated runs on identical code agree within 10 percent on M1.
- Gates fail loudly: injecting a 1 s stall into the pipeline makes the run exit non-zero.
- --compare prints baseline vs now with percentages.

title: Bench harness: synthetic multi-peer load generator (no DB, no deploy)
description:
Build scripts/bench: a scenario runner that reproduces a real room locally without Postgres, the API, or the web SPA.

Needed because every optimization in this epic must be provable with one local command, and today the only way to load the compositor is a full npm run dev plus two humans.

Components:
- Token minting straight from shared/join-token with SFU_JOIN_SECRET (issueJoinToken, role=compositor and role=speaker). No API, no DB.
- Synthetic peers: N headless Chrome instances (puppeteer, already a dependency) loading a minimal publisher page served by a ~20 line static server. Each joins the SFU via shared/sfu-client and publishes video+audio from --use-fake-device-for-media-stream, optionally --use-file-for-fake-video-capture=bench/pattern_1080p30.y4m (generated once with ffmpeg testsrc2, which is already a dependency) so the streams have real motion and cost real decode.
- Scenario driver: warmup, go-live (archive and/or live destination), layout/overlay churn, stop. Uses the existing internal HTTP API (POST /internal/rooms/:slug/warmup|go-live|layout|overlay|stop) with x-internal-secret.
- Scenario definitions S1-S6 from the epic design, selectable with --scenario, --peers, --stage, --rooms, --duration.
- Local live destination without new tools: write FLV to a file (ffmpeg -f flv out.flv) through the same tee path. Optional --rtmp=local uses mediamtx if the binary is present (dev-only, never in prod).
- npm run bench alias in the root package.json.

server/e2e.mjs is the prior art for driving headless Chrome against the stack; reuse its shape but drop the API/DB dependency.
design:
SCENARIO: all (this bead builds the generator).
TOGGLE: n/a.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 --duration=60 runs to completion with 15 joined peers (10 on scene), produces an archive file and an FLV file, and prints the session log path.
NOTES: must work on macOS (owner laptop) and Ubuntu 24.04 (the box). Must not require the API or Postgres. Must clean up every child process on exit and on SIGINT.
acceptance_criteria:
- npm run bench -- --scenario=S1 and --scenario=S2 both complete without manual steps.
- The compositor session log shows the expected number of sources on program.
- No orphaned Chrome or ffmpeg processes after the run.
- A README section in scripts/bench explains how to add a scenario.
notes: CORRECTNESS TRAP: streaming-cpg reports that producers arriving via the fire-and-forget newProducer push are silently lost (failures go to console.error). The bench spawns N peers AFTER the room exists, so it exercises exactly that path. If some peers are lost, the harness measures a fake win (fewer decodes = less CPU) and every M3/per-peer number is wrong. Acceptance addition: the harness must assert that all N expected producers were consumed and are actually delivering frames (count active video decoders / frames decoded in the recorder page and fail the run if it is below N). Same assertion belongs in the baseline run (t3).

title: Compositor GPU offload: <=0.8 core per room, 5 rooms per g4dn.xlarge, YouTube-clean 1080p30 live
description:
Move the compositor media path off the CPU and onto the GPU so one g4dn.xlarge (T4, 4 vCPU, 16 GB) can carry 4-5 rooms of 25 people (10 on stage) while streaming YouTube-clean 1080p30 live.

WHY (measured, from compositor/recordings/*.session.log):
- 2026-09-14T18:45 live session, 4m43s: 56.3 GB of raw pixels through the sink (199 MB/s), 8744 ffmpeg backpressure events, the archive received 663 video frames in 283 s (2.3 fps), the live FLV carried 11 s of media (speed=0.0389x).
- 2026-09-14T19:04: dropped_video=17445 vs video_frames=8150 (68 percent of frames dropped at the socket, queue 41 MB over a 33 MB cap), ffmpeg speed=0.44x.
- 2026-09-14T14:53: 30.9 GB moved, 1 video frame per 10 s window, host load 16.6 on 14 cores.
- On the prod box detectNvenc() failed (driver 595 NVENC API 13.0 vs BtbN latest built for 13.1), so every session silently fell back to MediaRecorder = OpenH264 SOFTWARE encode at 1080p60 and 25 Mbps. That fallback is the CPU bomb.

ROOT CAUSE (three separate ones):
1. ffmpeg is told -f rawvideo -r 60 while the wire delivers 2-24 fps. Dropped frames become stretched time, not dropped frames. That is the wrong-playback-speed bug, and it is unfixable without real timestamps.
2. Raw 1080p BGRA at 60 fps is 3.98 Gbps of memcpy: GPU readback, frame.copyTo, bytesToArrayBuffer (a second full copy), ws.send, Node Buffer, child.stdin.write, then ffmpeg swscale BGRA to yuv420p on CPU. Four copies plus a software colour conversion per frame.
3. sfu-client consumes and resumes EVERY producer in the room (no scene filter), and the router is VP8, which no NVIDIA NVDEC can decode. 15 people in a room means 15 software video decodes to draw the 10 that are on scene - and 5 rooms means 75 decodes where 50 would do.

Note gpu_compositing is already enabled on the box - compositing is NOT the problem. Decode, readback, swscale and encode are.

TARGET ARCHITECTURE:
peers --H.264--> Chromium (NVDEC/VAAPI decode, GPU canvas composite, pixels never leave the GPU)
  --> WebCodecs VideoEncoder prefer-hardware (H.264 High, 2 s GOP, 6 Mbps) + AudioEncoder Opus
  --> mp4-muxer fragmented MP4 --> ws (~1.5 MB/s, real pts)
  --> Node --> ffmpeg -c:v copy --> tee{ archive .webm , live .flv/RTMP }

DECISIONS LOCKED BY THE OWNER (2026-09-15):
- Box: g4dn.xlarge, must carry 4-5 rooms. Room shape: 15 people in the room, at most 10 active on the scene.
- 1080p30 default is acceptable (60 fps becomes opt-in).
- Output must follow YouTube live guidance: H.264 High, 1080p30, video 3-6 Mbps, AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo 128-256 kbps, GOP 2 s.
- If the box cannot hardware-encode: REFUSE to go live (loud 503). No silent degrade. Dev-only escape hatch allowed.
- Router moves VP8 -> H.264.
- nvidia-vaapi-driver + vainfo may be added to the compositor image (apt, no daemon, not in the media path).
- A high-quality muxer library in the recorder page is allowed (mp4-muxer, Vanilagy, MIT, fragmented MP4).
- The raw-frame/NVENC pipe gets DELETED once Chrome-side encode is proven. Keep the codebase clean.
- Verification must run locally without deploying; the owner has a YouTube key for a manual gate but prefers an automated local test.

CONSTRAINTS: keep Chromium; no Xvfb / no X server / no extra daemons in the media path (ANGLE gl-egl + ozone-headless is already correct); only standard tools (ffmpeg, apt packages, npm libs).
design:
METRIC VOCABULARY (every child bead quotes these names).

CPU / memory, sampled at 1 Hz over all compositor-owned processes (node + the whole Chromium tree + ffmpeg), attributed per room:
  M1 cpu.core_s_per_room_min   CPU-seconds per room-minute. TARGET <= 48 (0.8 core -> 5 rooms on 4 vCPU).
  M2 cpu.node_pct / cpu.renderer_pct / cpu.gpu_proc_pct / cpu.ffmpeg_pct   per-process breakdown.
  M3 cpu.per_peer_core         decode slope = (cpu at N=10 on-scene peers - cpu at N=0) / 10.
  M4 mem.mb_per_room           TARGET <= 1200 (5 rooms <= 6 GB of 16 GB).

Quality oracle (ffprobe over the archive .webm and the live .flv):
  Q1 vid.duration_ratio        container duration / wall-clock session duration. GATE 0.99-1.01.
  Q2 vid.eff_fps               frame count / duration. GATE >= 0.97 x target fps.
  Q3 vid.jitter_ms_p95         p95 abs(frame interval - 1/fps). GATE <= 8 ms.
  Q4 av.drift_ms               abs(audio duration - video duration) and first-pts delta. GATE <= 40 / <= 80 ms.
  Q5 drop.frames, drop.backpressure   GATE both 0.
  Q6 rtmp.speed                ffmpeg reported speed. GATE 0.98-1.02.
  Q7 stream.conformance        H.264 High, 1080p30, video 3-6 Mbps, AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo 128-256 kbps, GOP <= 2 s.

GPU (box only, nvidia-smi dmon -s u):
  G1 gpu.enc_pct > 0 during a live session.  G2 gpu.dec_pct > 0 with peers on stage.  G3 gpu.util_pct.

Capability (chrome://gpu featureStatus + boot-time trial encode):
  C1 enc.mode = hw|sw.  C2 enc.hw_api = videotoolbox|vaapi|none.  C3 dec.mode = hw|sw.

BENCH SCENARIOS:
  S1 solo     1 room, 1 stage peer, 120 s, archive only.
  S2 panel    1 room, 15 joined / 10 on scene, 300 s, archive + local FLV live.  <- the owner scenario
  S3 density  5 rooms x (15 joined / 10 on scene), 300 s. Locally run R rooms and extrapolate per-room.
  S4 churn    S1 + layout switch every 5 s + comment overlay every 10 s, 120 s.
  S5 live     S2 + RTMP destination (local: ffmpeg -f flv to a file; optional mediamtx for a real RTMP handshake).
  S6 youtube  MANUAL. 5 min to a real YouTube key with the owner, then read the YouTube Live dashboard.

COMMANDS:
  npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 --duration=300 --report=bench/out/S2.json
  npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 --compare=bench/out/baseline-S2.json
  ./scripts/verify-compositor-gpu.sh          (box; gains a hardware-encode section)
  ./scripts/verify-compositor-gpu-local.sh    (Mac)

TEST-ONE-AT-A-TIME RULE: every optimization lands behind an env toggle named in its own bead, with a bench scenario, a numeric gate, and a --compare run against the previous baseline. Flags and losing code paths are removed in the final cleanup bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- M1 <= 48 core_s per room-minute measured in S2 on the g4dn.xlarge (5 rooms concurrent in S3).
- Q1-Q7 all pass in S2 and S5 locally and on the box.
- C1 enc.mode=hw on the box (vaapi) and locally (videotoolbox); C3 dec.mode=hw on the box.
- G1 and G2 non-zero during a live session on the box.
- Go-live refuses with a clear error when no hardware encoder is present.
- The raw-frame/NVENC pipe is deleted; no dead code paths remain.
- One YouTube broadcast (S6) with no dropped frames and correct playback speed, confirmed in the YouTube dashboard.
- README GPU section and .env.example describe the new pipeline; CI bench gate is green.

title: Owner cannot hear guests; only owner audio reaches RTMP
description: Guests hear the owner, the owner does not hear guests, and YouTube gets only the owner's audio. The owner publishes before anyone joins so their producers arrive in the join response producers[] array; guest producers arrive later via the fire-and-forget newProducer push, which swallows failures into console.error and loses the producer permanently. Instrument produce/consume/playback end to end, fix the lost-producer race in SfuClient.join, retry blocked autoplay on the next gesture, and add self mute. Must not regress any anti-feedback invariant.
acceptance_criteria: SFU logs produce + newProducer fanout + consume per kind; sfu-client logs its silent skip branches; producers arriving before recvTransport are queued and drained; blocked play() retries on next user gesture; mic mute toggles the published capture track only; both voices present in the recording

title: Document and verify local quality-gate setup
description:
## Goal
Make the deterministic gate reproducible for another developer on a clean local environment.

## Requirements
- Document prerequisites, service startup, required ffmpeg/ffprobe tools, and the one-command invocation.
- Document what the gate validates and what it intentionally does not validate.
- Document artifact locations and common failure meanings.
- Document cleanup behavior and how to run the gate against the local stack only.
- Add or update package scripts without changing the production deployment path.

## Acceptance criteria
- The documented command works with the repository’s local setup flow.
- Documentation explicitly excludes AI review, overnight/soak checks, AWS, YouTube, and other external destinations.
- A clean local run produces a passing report and leaves no test browser/session/resource leak.

title: Create the quality-gate orchestrator and artifact contract
description:
## Goal
Provide one reliable local command that runs the deterministic checks and produces actionable machine-readable results.

## Requirements
- Add a root-level command for the deterministic quality gate.
- Preflight required local services and tools with clear errors.
- Run the required checks in a predictable order with bounded timeouts.
- Generate a per-run artifact directory containing a versioned JSON report, individual check results, browser logs, media metadata, and relevant session logs.
- Return exit code 0 only when all required hard checks pass; return non-zero for any product or infrastructure failure.
- Perform cleanup in all paths and avoid collisions with existing recordings.
- Keep the core path short enough for local development and document expected runtime.

## Acceptance criteria
- A developer can run one documented command and understand which contract check failed.
- The report identifies test run ID, room, browser/compositor versions where available, check names, measured values, thresholds, and pass/fail status.
- No check depends on an AI response, manual inspection, cloud service, or external network.

title: Cover deterministic compositor scenes and layout transitions
description:
## Goal
Catch regressions in scenes, layout solving, source selection, and rendering without making the main gate dependent on brittle pixel goldens.

## Requirements
- Cover the supported camera scene presets: focus, pip-left, pip-right, and grid.
- Exercise at least two deterministic participants and, where applicable, a deterministic screen-share source.
- Validate layout snapshots and geometric invariants: expected sources are present, placements stay within bounds, no invalid dimensions occur, and scene changes do not remove active media unexpectedly.
- Run each selected scene through the compositor browser renderer and recording path, or through a shared browser harness that uses the same compositor module.
- Include at least one transition while media is active.
- Use extracted-frame/non-black and source-presence checks as supporting output checks; do not make antialiasing-sensitive pixel equality the only oracle.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every supported preset is exercised by a deterministic test.
- A scene with missing sources, invalid placements, blank output, or a transition that breaks the compositor fails.
- The test records the layout snapshot and scene name associated with every failure.

title: Exercise and validate the local RTMP path
description:
## Goal
Prove that compositor output can be passed through the real local ffmpeg/RTMP path without contacting an external platform.

## Requirements
- Add a local loopback RTMP receiver suitable for the quality gate, preferably an optional quality-test Compose service or a documented local fixture.
- Start the compositor in its live/RTMP mode with the local receiver URL and the required H.264 recorder path.
- Use the real recording WebSocket, RecordingGateway, ffmpeg argument construction, and tee/single-destination behavior under test.
- Capture enough output at the receiver to inspect it with ffprobe.
- Validate received video/audio codecs, dimensions, duration, keyframes, and non-empty payload.
- Capture compositor session logs and ffmpeg diagnostics.

## Acceptance criteria
- The test fails if the local RTMP receiver gets no stream or an incomplete stream.
- The test fails if the RTMP output is missing H.264 video or AAC audio, cannot be probed, or has no usable duration/keyframe.
- The test uses only loopback/local infrastructure and requires no platform credentials.
- The RTMP receiver is stopped and cleaned up after every run.

title: Validate compositor recording media output
description:
## Goal
Exercise the real compositor recording path and objectively validate the generated media file.

## Requirements
- Start and stop a recording through the existing local recording flow after both speakers are publishing.
- Validate the resulting file with ffprobe/ffmpeg rather than file size alone.
- Assert that the expected video and audio streams exist, with valid codecs, dimensions, duration, frame count/keyframes, and timestamps.
- Assert that video is not entirely black/empty and audio is not silent.
- Validate that the mixed output contains the deterministic participant audio signals.
- Save ffprobe JSON, audio-analysis output, session logs, and a representative extracted frame in the artifact directory.
- Avoid pixel-perfect screenshots as the sole oracle.

## Acceptance criteria
- Missing video, missing audio, invalid duration, invalid dimensions, no usable keyframe, black/empty video, silent audio, or missing expected tones causes a hard failure.
- The checks use explicit tolerances suitable for local Chromium timing and the configured stream profile.
- The recording is stopped and temporary output is cleaned up on both pass and failure.

title: Add deterministic studio audio and feedback assertions
description:
## Goal
Prove the participant audio contract in real browser pages.

## Requirements
- Add a test-only, explicitly gated diagnostics path or equivalent browser instrumentation for remote peer and remote audio streams.
- Assert that each participant sees exactly one other participant and receives the other participant audio/video tracks.
- Measure remote audio signal using objective browser-side metrics such as RMS and dominant-frequency energy.
- Verify Alice receives Bob’s expected tone and Bob receives Alice’s expected tone.
- Verify Alice does not receive Alice’s tone and Bob does not receive Bob’s tone.
- Keep the interpretation precise: participants must hear one another; self-feedback is forbidden.
- Define tolerances in code and report measured values, not only pass/fail.

## Acceptance criteria
- The test fails when a remote track is absent, silent, or has the wrong identity/frequency.
- The test fails when a local participant’s own deterministic tone appears in that participant’s remote playback set.
- The test passes when both directions contain the expected signal and neither direction contains the sender’s own signal above the defined leakage threshold.
- Diagnostics are disabled for normal production sessions.

title: Build deterministic two-speaker browser harness
description:
## Goal
Create the local Puppeteer harness and deterministic media fixtures used by the quality gate.

## Requirements
- Reuse the existing registration, authentication, room join, and compositor warmup flow.
- Create two unique test users and a unique room per run.
- Inject deterministic media before the studio application requests getUserMedia.
- Alice and Bob must have distinct fixed audio signals and distinct deterministic canvas video.
- Do not use physical devices or rely on Chromium generic fake-device output.
- Wait on observable join/publish conditions rather than fixed sleeps wherever possible; retain bounded timeouts.
- Always close pages/browser and stop all synthetic tracks in a finally path.

## Acceptance criteria
- Both pages join the same room through the real local API and SFU.
- Both pages publish one audio and one video track.
- The harness can run without AWS, YouTube, or external network access.
- A failed run leaves a useful artifact bundle and exits non-zero.
- The media fixture identities, frequencies, dimensions, frame rate, and timing are fixed constants in the test code.

title: Deterministic local streaming quality gate
description:
## Objective
Create a fast, local, deterministic quality gate for the core streaming path. The gate must exercise two real browser speakers through the API, SFU, studio audio path, compositor, recording sink, and local RTMP-compatible output without depending on AWS, YouTube, external networks, or subjective human/AI judgment.

## In scope
- Two synthetic browser participants joining one unique room.
- Deterministic audio and video tracks injected into the browser.
- Objective proof of bidirectional audio delivery.
- Objective proof that a participant does not receive their own microphone back.
- Objective proof that compositor video and mixed audio are present in the recorded output.
- Objective validation that the output can traverse the local ffmpeg/RTMP path.
- Deterministic scene/layout coverage for the compositor.
- Structured failure artifacts and one local command with a non-zero exit code on failure.

## Out of scope
- AI-based judging, diagnosis, or approval.
- Overnight agents, scheduled runs, or long-running soak tests.
- Real YouTube/AWS/platform credentials.
- Pixel-perfect screenshots as the sole pass/fail oracle.
- Performance/load testing beyond detecting an unusable or incomplete media output.

## Design constraints
- Reuse the existing Puppeteer dependency and current server/e2e.mjs flow unless a clear reason requires otherwise.
- Use synthetic, identity-specific signals rather than Chromium's generic fake camera/microphone devices: for example, distinct fixed audio tones and deterministic canvas video.
- Use thresholds and invariants checked by code; do not make pass/fail depend on an LLM or a human watching the recording.
- The core gate should be short enough for local development, with a documented target of approximately one minute once services are running.
- Tests must clean up browser pages, media tracks, recording sessions, and temporary files after success or failure.

## Required contract
1. Alice and Bob both join the same room and publish audio/video.
2. Alice receives Bob's audio and Bob receives Alice's audio.
3. Alice does not receive Alice's audio and Bob does not receive Bob's audio; this is specifically the local studio self-feedback invariant, while each participant must still be audible to the other.
4. The compositor receives participant video, generates a valid recording containing video and mixed audio, and produces output accepted by the local RTMP/ffmpeg path.

## Acceptance criteria
- A single documented local command runs the deterministic gate against the local stack.
- The command exits 0 only when all required hard checks pass.
- The gate fails for missing participants, missing tracks, silent/unidentified remote audio, self-audio feedback, missing/invalid video, missing/invalid audio, invalid duration/format, or failed local RTMP output.
- The gate emits machine-readable results and enough logs/media metadata to identify which contract failed.
- The test uses no external streaming service and no cloud credentials.
- Running the gate twice with the same code and environment produces the same pass/fail contract; timing tolerances may account for startup latency but may not hide missing media.

title: Density validation on the T4: 5 rooms, pool model, admission control
description:
The actual business question: does one g4dn.xlarge carry 4-5 rooms of 15 people (10 on scene) at 1080p30 with clean YouTube output?

On the box (or extrapolated locally with R rooms and a per-room figure):
- Run S3: 5 concurrent rooms, each 15 joined / 10 on scene, 300 s, archive + live FLV. Record M1 per room, M4, host CPU, GPU util/enc/dec, and every Q gate for every room.
- Memory check: 5 x Chromium plus 5 x ffmpeg plus Node in 16 GB. If per-room memory exceeds ~1.2 GB, 5 rooms will not fit regardless of CPU.
- Pool model decision, measured both ways: 5 separate Chromium browsers (current model: strong isolation, 5 GPU processes, more RAM) versus 1 browser with 5 tabs (one GPU process, shared GL context, cheaper, but one renderer crash or one runaway tab can take several rooms). Report M1, M4 and the blast radius, then pick.
- Admission control: warmup/go-live must refuse when the box is over budget (free slots AND a CPU/memory budget), instead of accepting a 6th room and degrading all 6. Expose the budget and the current load in /internal/health so the API can route new rooms to another box.
- Identify the binding constraint: if NVENC or NVDEC saturates before the CPU does, say so explicitly - then the lever is output resolution/fps per room, fewer rooms per box, or a bigger GPU (g5.xlarge A10G), not more code optimization.

Deliverable: a short capacity report on the epic (rooms per box, the binding constraint, the recommended pool model, the admission thresholds) plus the code for admission control.
design:
SCENARIO: S3.
METRIC: M1 per room, M4, host CPU percent, G1/G2/G3, all Q gates per room.
GATE: 5 rooms x (15 joined / 10 on scene) hold M1 <= 48 core_s per room-minute, every room passes Q1-Q7, host CPU < 90 percent, no OOM, no room starved.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S3 --rooms=5 --duration=300 on the box with nvidia-smi dmon -s u and the monitor container running; capacity report attached to the epic.
acceptance_criteria:
- S3 runs 5 concurrent rooms with all quality gates passing in each.
- A capacity report states rooms per box, the binding constraint (CPU, NVDEC, NVENC or RAM) and the evidence.
- The pool model (browsers vs tabs) is decided from measurements, with the blast radius noted.
- Admission control refuses new rooms over budget and /internal/health exposes the load signal.

title: Hardware video decode on the box: NVDEC through VAAPI in Chromium
description:
Make the decode side of Chromium run on NVDEC using the env, packages and flags proven in t5. Without this, 50 software H.264 decodes across 5 rooms cannot fit in 4 vCPU no matter how good the encode path is.

Changes:
- compositor/Dockerfile: install nvidia-vaapi-driver (and keep vainfo for diagnostics, it is tiny and not in the media path).
- compose.gpu.yml: LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia, LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/dri, NVD_BACKEND=direct, and NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES already includes video.
- compositor/src/browser/gpu.ts chromeGpuArgs: add the VAAPI decode feature flags that t5 found necessary for this Chromium version (names have changed across releases - use what the spike recorded, not folklore), keeping --use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl.
- Extend the t4 probe so C3 dec.mode is asserted the same way compositing is, and section 10 of the verify script reports the decoder verdict and nvidia-smi decoder percentage.
- Failure policy: with COMPOSITOR_GPU_STRICT=1 a software decoder must be fatal at boot; otherwise it is logged, reported in health, and counted against the density recommendation (5 rooms assumes hardware decode).

Local Mac note: VideoToolbox decode is already hardware there, so this bead is box-only; the bench gate is measured on the T4.
design:
SCENARIO: S2 and S3 on the box.
METRIC: C3 dec.mode, M3, G2 gpu.dec_pct, M1.
GATE: chrome://gpu video_decode = Hardware accelerated; G2 > 0 during S2; M3 down >= 60 percent versus software decode; C3 reported in /internal/health.
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_HW_DECODE=1|0.
PROOF: on the box, npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 with the toggle on and off while nvidia-smi dmon -s u runs; compare M3 and G2; ./scripts/verify-compositor-gpu.sh section 10.
acceptance_criteria:
- nvidia-vaapi-driver installed and the LIBVA/NVD env set in compose.gpu.yml.
- chrome://gpu reports hardware video decode; /internal/health exposes dec.mode.
- M3 drops >= 60 percent with hardware decode on the box.
- The verify script reports the decode verdict.
- Strict mode makes a software decoder fatal when COMPOSITOR_GPU_STRICT=1.

title: Scene-filtered consumption: decode only the sources that are on program
description:
shared/sfu-client consumes and resumes EVERY producer it sees (join() loops over joined.producers, newProducer triggers consumeProducer, and the consumer is resumed immediately). There is no scene filter. With 15 people in the room and at most 10 on scene, the compositor decodes 5 streams that are never drawn, and mixes their mics into the recording. Across 5 rooms that is 25 wasted decodes on a single T4.

Changes:
- shared/sfu-client: add a subscription policy - consume lazily and expose setDesiredSources(ids) that resumes matching consumers and pauses (or closes, after a grace period) the rest. mediasoup consumers start paused already; keep them paused rather than creating and destroying where possible, so a source coming on scene is instant.
- compositor/page/src/CompositorPage.tsx: feed the policy from the layout state (the same state that setLayout receives, and getLayoutSnapshot already computes the effective sources).
- Audio: only on-scene mics enter the recording mix. PRODUCT QUESTION TO CONFIRM WITH THE OWNER IN THIS BEAD: should backstage mics ever be audible on the recording or the live stream? Today every joined peer mic is mixed in, which means a backstage conversation can leak into a broadcast. Default assumption for this bead: NO - program audio is on-scene audio only.
- The studio can reuse the same policy for its grid (viewers then decode fewer streams too) - do that only if it does not regress the backstage UX; otherwise ship it recorder-side first.
- Log the subscription set changes to the session log so a missing tile is diagnosable.

Measure the slope: M3 with 15 joined / 10 on scene must match M3 with 10 joined / 10 on scene within 10 percent.
design:
SCENARIO: S2 (15 joined, 10 on scene) and a variant with 10 joined.
METRIC: M1, M3, number of active video decoders (log it), audio mix membership.
GATE: M1 for 15 joined / 10 on scene within 10 percent of M1 for 10 joined / 10 on scene; no off-scene mic in the recording (verify by giving off-scene peers a distinctive tone in the bench and checking the archive audio).
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_SCENE_FILTER=1|0.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 --compare=<previous> with the toggle on and off; ffprobe/inspect the archive audio for the off-scene tone.
acceptance_criteria:
- Off-scene producers are never resumed by the recorder (logged and measured).
- A source coming on scene appears within one layout update, with no blank-tile window longer than ~200 ms.
- Off-scene microphones are not in the recording (owner-confirmed policy recorded in the bead).
- M1 for 15/10 matches 10/10 within 10 percent.

title: Ship the H.264 router and publisher configuration
description:
Implement the t17 decision.

- sfu/src/mediasoup/mediasoup.service.ts: MEDIA_CODECS per the spike (H.264 preferred, VP8 secondary only if the spike says so).
- shared/sfu-client/src/index.ts publish(): the codecOptions currently set videoGoogleStartBitrate, which is VP8/libvpx-specific. Replace with the right H.264 knobs (start bitrate via videoGoogleStartBitrate is still honoured by Chrome for H.264, but confirm) and set maxBitrate from the profile chosen in t20.
- web/src/hooks/useStudioSession.ts getUserMedia constraints and any codec preference (degradedPreference, contentHint for screen share: detail vs motion).
- The compositor consumes whatever the router negotiates; confirm the recorder page logs the negotiated codec per consumer so a VP8 fallback is visible in the session log.
- Existing rooms: routers are per-room and lazily created, so a restart is sufficient. Document that a codec change requires an SFU restart and that in-flight rooms must be drained.

Gate is that nothing regresses: the studio still works in Chrome and Safari, the e2e smoke passes, and the bench scenarios run green with H.264.
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S5 plus server/e2e.mjs.
METRIC: negotiated codec per consumer (logged), M3, Q1-Q7.
GATE: every on-scene consumer negotiates H.264 in the bench; Q gates unchanged; e2e passes; studio preview unaffected in Chrome and Safari.
TOGGLE: SFU_VIDEO_CODECS=h264|vp8|h264+vp8 (env on the SFU) so the change is reversible without a rebuild.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 with each codec setting; server/e2e.mjs green.
acceptance_criteria:
- The router negotiates H.264 for camera and screen producers.
- The negotiated codec is logged per consumer in the compositor session log.
- server/e2e.mjs passes; the studio works in Chrome and Safari.
- The codec choice is env-switchable for rollback.

title: SPIKE: SFU router VP8 -> H.264 (packetization-mode 1) and the browser matrix
description:
VP8 cannot be hardware-decoded on any NVIDIA GPU (NVDEC has no VP8 path), so keeping VP8 guarantees software decode for all 50 on-scene streams across 5 rooms. H.264 also matches the RTMP output and is what Safari and iOS prefer to publish.

Spike, locally and on the box:
- sfu/src/mediasoup/mediasoup.service.ts MEDIA_CODECS: add video/H264 with clockRate 90000, parameters packetization-mode=1, profile-level-id that permits 1080p30 High (e.g. 640c1f / 640028 - confirm what Chrome and mediasoup negotiate), level-asymmetry-allowed=1. Check whether video/rtx is needed alongside it.
- Confirm the mediasoup version in sfu/package.json supports H.264 routing and that router.canConsume succeeds between a publisher and the compositor consumer.
- Publisher hardware encode: read chrome://webrtc-internals on a real Chrome (macOS VideoToolbox, Windows Media Foundation, Linux VAAPI) and confirm the outbound encoder is hardware. If a target browser falls back to OpenH264 software, compare its CPU with what VP8 cost - OpenH264 is usually cheaper than libvpx, so this is likely a win even in the fallback case, but measure it.
- Browser matrix: Chrome desktop, Safari desktop, iOS Safari, Android Chrome, Firefox. Record which publish and which consume H.264. Decide whether VP8 stays in the codec list as a secondary for stragglers (recommended: yes, with H.264 preferred, and the compositor refusing a VP8 consumer for on-scene sources if that would mean software decode - or accepting it and reporting it).
- Rollback plan: routers are created per room lazily, so reverting MEDIA_CODECS and restarting the SFU is enough; no migration.

Output: a decision note with the exact MEDIA_CODECS array, the negotiated profile-level-id, the browser matrix, and whether VP8 stays as a fallback.
design:
SCENARIO: S2 with the H.264 router (bench peers are headless Chrome, so they follow the router).
METRIC: C3 dec.mode, M3 cpu.per_peer_core, G2 gpu.dec_pct, publisher-side encode CPU.
GATE: a written verdict plus a measured M3 with H.264 versus VP8 on the same scenario.
PROOF: two S2 runs (VP8 router, H.264 router) compared with --compare; on the box, nvidia-smi decoder percentage during the H.264 run.
NOTES: this spike does not have to wait for the encode work - it can run in parallel once the harness (t1/t2) and the baseline (t3) exist.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exact MEDIA_CODECS array and negotiated profile-level-id recorded.
- Chrome publisher confirmed hardware-encoding H.264 (webrtc-internals evidence).
- Browser matrix filled in for publish and consume.
- Decision on keeping VP8 as a secondary codec, with rationale.
- M3 measured for H.264 vs VP8 on the box.

title: Delete the raw-frame/NVENC pipe and the MediaRecorder fallback
description:
The owner wants the codebase clean: one encode path, not three.

Delete once t12/t13/t14 are proven:
- compositor/src/recordings/raw-pipe.ts, raw-pipe.spec.ts, nvenc.ts, nvenc.spec.ts
- compositor/page/src/nvenc-pipe.ts and its VIDEO_FORMAT_CODES duplication
- the codec=raw branch in recording.gateway.ts (handleRawNvenc and its helpers, the extraStdin fd3 plumbing, MAX_PENDING_AUDIO_BYTES, VIDEO_WAIT_WARN_MS)
- the MediaRecorder path in compositor/page/src/CompositorPage.tsx, plus pickRecorderFormat / H264_RECORDER_FORMATS / FALLBACK_RECORDER_FORMATS / parseRecorderCodec in shared/stream-quality IF nothing else uses them (grep the studio first - web/ does not record, but confirm)
- COMPOSITOR_NVENC from .env.example, compositor/.env, compose.yml, README
- the GpuEncodeMode type and the encode=mediarecorder|nvenc vocabulary, replaced by enc.mode/enc.hw_api from t4

CONTINGENCY: if t5 returned outcome B (VAAPI decode works, encode does not), do NOT delete the raw path - instead retitle this bead and ship the corrected raw fallback (per-frame pts with -vsync vfr, NV12 pinned, single copy, 1080p30). Record which branch was taken on the epic.

After deletion: typecheck, unit tests, lint (oxlint), and a full S1/S2/S5 bench run to prove nothing regressed.
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S5.
METRIC: all gates must still pass; lines of code removed.
GATE: npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run lint clean in compositor and shared; S1/S2/S5 gates unchanged from t16; grep finds no reference to raw/nvenc/MediaRecorder in the compositor.
TOGGLE: n/a (this bead removes the toggles that lost).
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 --compare=<previous> after deletion.
acceptance_criteria:
- Only one encode path remains in the repository.
- Dead env vars, types, specs and docs are gone.
- typecheck, tests and lint pass; S1/S2/S5 gates still pass.
- README and .env.example describe the single remaining path.

title: Go-live refuses when the video encoder is not hardware
description:
The owner decision: refuse, do not degrade. The current behaviour is the reason a whole broadcast went out software-encoded at 25 Mbps - detectNvenc failed, the pool logged a warning, and go-live proceeded on OpenH264 at 1080p60, which cannot keep up.

Changes:
- compositor/src/sessions/sessions.service.ts goLive: consult the capability probe (t4). When enc.mode != hw, throw 503 with a message that names the fix (run scripts/verify-compositor-gpu.sh, check nvidia-vaapi-driver and the LIBVA env, check the Chromium version) instead of a generic failure. Write the refusal to the session log.
- The API surface: server/src/recordings must pass the compositor refusal through as a readable 503 to the studio, and the studio must show it (not a spinner that never resolves).
- COMPOSITOR_ALLOW_SOFTWARE_ENCODE=1 as a dev-only escape hatch (local runs without a GPU, CI). When set, log it loudly at boot, in the session log and in /internal/health, and cap the profile to something OpenH264 can actually sustain (720p30, <= 3 Mbps) so a dev box does not reproduce the same slow-motion failure.
- warmup may stay permissive (a warm slot with no encode is harmless); the refusal belongs at go-live.
design:
SCENARIO: S5 with the encoder forced to software (COMPOSITOR_ENCODE=mediarecorder or prefer-software) and with hardware.
METRIC: C1 enc.mode, HTTP status of go-live.
GATE: software => go-live returns 503 with an actionable message and no recording is produced; hardware => go-live proceeds; with the dev override the session runs at the capped profile and the log says so.
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_ALLOW_SOFTWARE_ENCODE=0|1.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S5 twice (forced software, then hardware) and check the status codes and the session logs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Go-live returns 503 with an actionable message when no hardware encoder is present.
- The studio surfaces the refusal to the user.
- Dev override exists, is loud, and caps resolution/bitrate.
- Refusal and override are recorded in the session log and /internal/health.

title: Audio path: remove the per-sample JS interleave and prove A/V sync
description:
The raw pipe converts every AudioData by allocating a Float32Array per plane, calling copyTo per plane, then running two per-sample loops to interleave (and a fallback path with another per-sample loop). At 48 kHz stereo that is ~192k float writes per second per room in JS, plus a GC allocation per chunk. The 2026-09-14 14:53 log shows ~1946 audio packets per second reaching the sink, i.e. very small chunks and therefore very high per-packet overhead.

Changes:
- If t12 lands first, audio goes through AudioEncoder (Opus) and these loops disappear entirely - do this bead in whichever order the dependency graph allows, but do not optimize code that is about to be deleted. If t12 is not yet in, replace the interleave with a single copyTo into an interleaved f32 buffer where the format allows it, otherwise a tight typed-array copy with a stride, and reuse one buffer per stream instead of allocating per chunk.
- Batch audio to ~20-40 ms per packet to cut per-packet overhead on the wire and in the gateway.
- Keep the Web Audio mix (gain -> limiter -> MediaStreamDestination) as it is: it is cheap and it is what gives one mixed track per room. Keep the 48 kHz assertion in ensureAudio.
- Add an explicit A/V sync measurement to the bench oracle if t2 does not already cover it (first audio pts vs first video pts, and duration delta).

The 25 Mbps recorder profile change in t6 does not touch audio; this bead is the audio half of the quality story (the owner reported crackle and speed problems historically).
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S5.
METRIC: M2 cpu.renderer_pct, Q4 av.drift_ms, audio packets per second.
GATE: Q4 <= 40 ms duration delta and <= 80 ms first-pts delta; renderer CPU down measurably; audio packets per second <= 60 at 20 ms batching (i.e. ~50/s).
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_AUDIO=batched|legacy (or =encoder once t12 exists).
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S5 --compare=<previous>; listen to 10 s of the archive; ffprobe the audio and video stream start times.
acceptance_criteria:
- No per-sample JS loops remain in the audio path (or the path is deleted by t12).
- Audio batched to 20-40 ms; packet rate logged.
- Q4 gates pass in S1, S2 and S5.
- The 48 kHz AudioContext assertion still fires loudly on mismatch.

title: Cache text rendering and memoize layout solves in the compositor draw loop
description:
Every frame, for every tile, drawLabel sets ctx.font, calls wrapTextLines with a measureText callback per candidate line, measures each wrapped line again, then draws a rounded box and the glyphs. drawCommentOverlay does the same for the overlay. At 30 fps with 10 tiles that is thousands of measureText calls per second on the main thread, and 2D canvas text is one of the few parts of the draw that is genuinely expensive on the CPU side even when the canvas is GPU accelerated.

Changes in shared/canvas-compositor/src/index.ts (+ wrap-text.ts, layout.ts):
- Render each label once per (name, font, maxWidth, maxHeight) into a cached OffscreenCanvas and blit it with drawImage. Invalidate on name change or resize. Same for the comment overlay card (invalidate on author/text/size change; the overlay already expires on until).
- Memoize layoutSolve on a signature of (layoutState, sorted source ids + kinds + aspect ratios, width, height) so an unchanged scene does not re-solve 30 times a second.
- Hoist ctx.font / fillStyle assignments out of the per-tile loop where possible (each font assignment invalidates internal state).
- Keep the diagnostic logging behind a flag - the per-peer console.log every 2 s also costs (string building + CDP console forwarding to Node).

The studio preview shares this module, so the caching must be correct there too (name edits, layout switches, window resize).
design:
SCENARIO: S4 (churn) primarily, S1/S2 for regression.
METRIC: M2 cpu.renderer_pct, CDP ScriptDuration/LayoutDuration/RecalcStyleDuration from Performance.getMetrics.
GATE: S4 renderer CPU down >= 40 percent; S1/S2 unchanged or better; Q1-Q7 unchanged; the studio layout tests (shared/canvas-compositor/src/layout.test.ts) still pass and label text is pixel-identical to the uncached version in a bench snapshot.
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_TEXT_CACHE=1|0, COMPOSITOR_LAYOUT_MEMO=1|0.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S4 --compare=<previous>, with the toggles flipped to attribute the win.
acceptance_criteria:
- Labels and the overlay are drawn from cached bitmaps; cache invalidation covered by unit tests.
- layoutSolve memoized with a correct signature; existing layout tests pass.
- S4 renderer CPU down >= 40 percent; pixel snapshot of a label matches the uncached render.
- Diagnostic logging is behind a flag and off by default.

title: Draw-on-demand: captureStream(0) + requestFrame, rVFC-driven redraw, rAF probe
description:
shared/canvas-compositor/src/index.ts currently drives a chained setTimeout at 1000/fps and captures with canvas.captureStream(fps). Two problems:
1. captureStream(fps) is timer based, so frames are emitted whether or not the canvas changed - duplicate frames go to the encoder, and the capture cadence can beat the draw cadence.
2. The comment in the code says rAF does not fire in headless Chromium. That is true for chrome-headless-shell, but puppeteer 25 launches --headless=new, which has a real viz BeginFrame source. Worth a 5-line probe: if rAF fires, it paces the loop to the compositor instead of drifting against it.

Changes:
- Probe rAF in --headless=new (log the measured callback rate for 5 s). Use rAF when it fires at the expected rate, keep the chained setTimeout as the fallback, and record which one is active in the session log.
- Switch to canvas.captureStream(0) and call canvas.requestFrame() once per drawn frame, so the capture track contains exactly the frames we drew, with the timestamps Chrome assigns at request time.
- Drive redraw from requestVideoFrameCallback on the source video elements: when no source produced a new frame and neither the layout nor the overlay changed, skip the draw (but still request a frame at the target cadence so the output stays CFR for YouTube).
- Compensate timer drift when setTimeout is used (schedule against an absolute clock, not 1000/fps after the previous draw finished).

The 2026-09-14 18:45 log shows the draw loop actually produced ~24 fps while captureStream was set to 60 - i.e. 60 percent of captured frames were duplicates.
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S4.
METRIC: M2 cpu.renderer_pct, Q2, Q3, frames-captured-per-second vs frames-drawn-per-second (log both).
GATE: renderer CPU down >= 30 percent in S2; Q2 eff_fps >= 0.97 x target; Q3 jitter p95 <= 8 ms; captured frames == drawn frames (no duplicates).
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_CAPTURE=requestframe|timer, COMPOSITOR_REDRAW=ondemand|always, COMPOSITOR_LOOP=raf|timeout.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S4 --compare=<previous report>; repeat with the toggles flipped to isolate each half of the change.
acceptance_criteria:
- rAF probe result recorded (fires / does not fire in --headless=new) and the chosen loop logged at session start.
- captureStream(0) + requestFrame is the default; captured == drawn frames.
- Redraw skipped when nothing changed, output still CFR.
- S4 renderer CPU down >= 30 percent versus the previous baseline; Q2/Q3 pass.

title: Stop painting the program canvas: detach it, shrink the viewport, A/B desynchronized
description:
The recorder page appends the 1920x1080 program canvas to the document with style width 100 percent, and the page viewport is set to 1920x1080 in sessions.service.ts warmup. So every drawn frame is rasterized, composited and presented to a display nobody watches, on top of being captured. In headless that still costs a viz frame, a raster pass and a swap.

Changes:
- shared/canvas-compositor: add an option (attach: false / detached canvas) so the recorder never appends the canvas. The studio preview MUST keep appending it - the module is shared, so this is an option, not a behaviour change. Verify captureStream works on a canvas that is not in the document (it captures the backing store, so it does; prove it in the bench).
- compositor/page/src/CompositorPage.tsx: keep only the small status line in the DOM; do not append the program canvas.
- compositor/src/sessions/sessions.service.ts: setViewport to something small (e.g. 320x240) - the viewport no longer has to match the output resolution.
- A/B the 2D context attributes: desynchronized true can force a low-latency path that bypasses the normal swap chain and is slower on some drivers; alpha false should stay (opaque backing store is what enables the GPU 2D path).

Watch out: the page still needs a working compositor for WebRTC video elements and Web Audio; a 0x0 or display:none page can trigger occlusion throttling, which is why --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows is already set. Measure, do not assume.
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2.
METRIC: M2 cpu.gpu_proc_pct, cpu.renderer_pct, M1.
GATE: M1 down >= 10 percent in S2 with no change to Q1-Q7 (the pixels captured must be identical - compare a screenshot of the canvas via readback in the bench to catch a blank-frame regression).
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_CANVAS=detached|attached, COMPOSITOR_VIEWPORT=320x240|1920x1080, COMPOSITOR_CANVAS_DESYNC=0|1.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 --compare=<previous>; plus a pixel-diff check that the detached canvas still produces the expected frame content.
acceptance_criteria:
- The recorder canvas is not in the document and still captures correct frames (pixel check in the bench).
- The studio preview is unaffected (it still attaches its canvas).
- Viewport is small in the recorder page; M1 down >= 10 percent.
- desynchronized A/B result recorded and the winner kept.

title: Frame budget: 1080p30 default and YouTube-aligned bitrates
description:
Cheapest large win, and it makes every later measurement cheaper too: the profile is 1080p60 with recorderVideoBps 25 Mbps and rtmpVideoBitrate 12000k, which is above YouTube guidance for live and doubles every cost in the pipeline (decode is unaffected, but composite, capture, encode and mux all halve).

Changes:
- shared/stream-quality/src/profiles.ts: fps 60 -> 30; recorderVideoBps 25_000_000 -> 6_000_000; rtmpVideoBitrate 12000k -> 6000k; rtmpMaxrate 13000k -> 7000k; rtmpBufsize 24000k -> 12000k; rtmpAudioBitrate 256k -> 192k; ffmpegPreset only matters on the (doomed) re-encode path.
- shared/stream-quality: GOP stays fps*2 = 60 frames = 2 s, which is the YouTube live keyframe recommendation.
- Anywhere fps is used for scheduling or capture (shared/canvas-compositor draw loop, canvas.captureStream, nvenc/raw GOP math) picks the profile value up automatically - verify none of them hard-code 60.
- Add COMPOSITOR_FPS (default 30, 60 opt-in) and COMPOSITOR_VIDEO_KBPS so the A/B is a flag, not a rebuild.

YouTube live guidance for 1080p30: video 3,000-6,000 kbps, H.264 High, AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo, GOP 2 s. 6 Mbps is the top of the range: best quality inside the guideline.

This bead must NOT change the encode path - it only changes the frame budget and the bitrates. It is measurable on its own.
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S5.
METRIC: M1, M2, Q2, Q7.
GATE: M1 down >= 40 percent versus the t3 baseline in S2; Q2 eff_fps >= 0.97 x 30; Q7 conformance passes (H.264 High, 1080p30, 3-6 Mbps, GOP <= 2 s).
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_FPS=30|60, COMPOSITOR_VIDEO_KBPS.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 --compare=bench/out/baseline-S2.json, then the same run with COMPOSITOR_FPS=60 to show the delta is caused by this change.
acceptance_criteria:
- 30 fps is the default everywhere (profile, draw loop, capture, GOP).
- Bitrates match YouTube 1080p30 guidance and Q7 passes.
- S2 M1 is at least 40 percent below baseline, proven with --compare and with the 60 fps toggle.
- No hard-coded 60 remains (grep + unit test on the profile).

title: Guests see their own camera instead of the program preview
description: The program preview is composited client-side from LayoutState, which is local per client and only fanned out from owner to the recorder. A guest falls through to DEFAULT_LAYOUT (focus preset, featuredId auto-set to their own camera) and focus renders only the featured source, so they see nothing but themselves. Apply the owner's broadcast layout on non-owner clients and stop their local auto-feature effect from fighting it.
acceptance_criteria: Owner layout/preset/feature changes appear in the guest preview; guest preset buttons stay inert; a reloading guest lands on the owner's layout, not their own camera

title: Guests see owner-only Start recording / Go live buttons
description: StudioHeader renders Start recording and Go live to every peer. The server rejects non-owners (requireOwnerBySlug), so a guest clicking them just gets 403 red text. Gate both on isOwner and give guests a read-only REC/LIVE status pill driven by the synced roomState, with an elapsed timer anchored to the owner's startedAt.
acceptance_criteria: Guest header shows no Start recording / Go live; guest sees REC/LIVE pill with elapsed time matching owner; guest can leave during owner's recording without the navigation blocker; comments column stays owner-only

title: roomState relay over /ws/signaling
description: Owner session state (layout + recording/live status) never reaches guests. Add a roomState request/event to the SFU signaling protocol: owner (canManage) publishes, SFU validates + caches per room + relays to other peers, and the cached state rides in the join response so late joiners are correct immediately. Shared prerequisite for the guest-controls and program-preview bugs.
acceptance_criteria: SFU relays roomState only from canManage peers; cached state returned in join payload; cache cleared on closeRoom and when the room empties; parseRoomState unit-tested

title: CI bench gate: fail on CPU regression or any quality gate
description:
The harness is only useful if it runs without a human remembering to.

- A CI job that runs a short S1 and S5 (60 s each) on the Mac runner (VideoToolbox gives real hardware encode, so the primary path is exercised) and fails on: M1 more than 10 percent above the committed reference baseline, or any Q1-Q7 gate, or enc.mode != hw.
- The reference baseline is a committed bench/out/ci-baseline.json, updated deliberately (a PR that changes it must say why).
- Box-only metrics (G1-G3, vaapi) cannot run in CI - keep them in scripts/verify-compositor-gpu.sh and make that script part of the deploy checklist, printing a clear PASS/FAIL.
- Keep the job under ~5 minutes: 60 s scenarios plus startup, one room, few peers.
- Existing unit tests (compositor npm test, shared layout tests) stay in the same job.
design:
SCENARIO: S1 and S5, shortened.
METRIC: M1 versus the committed baseline, all Q gates, enc.mode.
GATE: CI red when a deliberate 15 percent CPU regression or a broken frame timing is introduced; green on main.
PROOF: introduce a temporary regression in a branch and watch CI fail; revert and watch it pass.
acceptance_criteria:
- CI runs the short bench and the unit tests on every change.
- A >10 percent M1 regression or any Q gate failure fails the build.
- The reference baseline is committed and changes require an explicit reason.
- The verify script remains the box-side gate and is in the deploy checklist.

title: Observability: per-room CPU, fps, drops and codec in health, session log and README
description:
Everything learned in this epic must be visible without SSH, or the next regression will be diagnosed from YouTube comments again.

- /internal/health: per-room enc.mode/hw_api, dec.mode, negotiated consumer codecs, effective output fps, dropped frames, backpressure events, wire kbps, CPU-seconds per room-minute, RSS, plus the box-level budget from t23.
- Session log: keep the ingress window stats, add the encode-side counters (frames in, frames encoded, key frames, queue-depth drops) and the capability verdict at go-live.
- compose.yml monitor container: it already writes docker stats and nvidia-smi into recordings/diagnostics/host-stats.log every 15 s - extend it to also poll /internal/health so the per-room numbers land in the same file for post-mortems.
- README: rewrite the Compositor GPU section for the new pipeline (it currently documents h264_nvenc and the raw pipe), the YouTube output settings, the capacity figure from t23, the nvidia-vaapi-driver requirement, and the new env vars. Update .env.example and compose.yml comments to match.
- scripts/verify-compositor-gpu.sh: make sure the sections still tell the truth after the deletions in t15 (it currently checks for encode=nvenc).
design:
SCENARIO: S2, S5.
METRIC: presence and correctness of every field above.
GATE: a live session can be fully diagnosed from /internal/health and the session log alone; the verify script passes on the box; README matches the shipped env vars.
PROOF: run S5, then curl /internal/health and cat the session log; run ./scripts/verify-compositor-gpu.sh.
acceptance_criteria:
- /internal/health reports per-room encode/decode mode, fps, drops, backpressure, kbps, CPU and memory.
- The monitor container records the same per-room numbers to diagnostics.
- The verify script is updated and passes on the box.
- README, .env.example and compose.yml describe the shipped pipeline, with no reference to deleted paths.

title: Simulcast layers + setPreferredLayers from tile geometry (conditional on S3 failing)
description:
CONDITIONAL: do this only if S3 still misses the density gate after t19 (scene filter), t20 (ingest cap) and t21 (hardware decode). With 10 on-scene tiles per room, most of them ~380x216, decoding one full-resolution stream per tile is the remaining waste; layers let each tile decode only the pixels it displays.

If it is needed:
- Publisher: two simulcast layers (e.g. 720p + 360p, or 1080p + 360p depending on t20) via mediasoup encodings with scalabilityMode; keep the layer count at 2, not 3 - each extra layer is another encode session on a speaker laptop.
- SFU: expose setPreferredLayers through signaling (a new method next to resumeConsumer) so a consumer can be pinned to a layer.
- Compositor: map placement geometry from layout.ts (w/h per source) to a layer, and re-pin on every layout change (focus -> high layer, grid -> low layer). Handle the ~1 GOP delay when a peer is promoted to focus: pre-pin the high layer for peers that are one click away from being featured, or accept the pop and measure it.
- Studio: the grid can use the low layer too, which cuts viewer bandwidth and laptop CPU - a product win, not only a compositor one.

Consequences to measure and report before shipping (the owner asked for these explicitly):
- Speaker device: one extra encode session (hardware where available), roughly +10-20 percent uplink, more battery/heat; on a low-end device or a browser without hardware H.264 encode this is real CPU.
- SFU box: more forwarded bytes per producer (~+15 percent) and slightly more per-consumer work.
- Viewers: less bandwidth and less decode for grids; quality pop on layer switches.
- Compositor: the win - decode pixels per room drop by roughly the tile-area ratio (about 9x for a 10-tile grid).

If the measurement says the trade is not worth it, close this bead with the numbers and keep t20 as the answer.
design:
SCENARIO: S2, S3.
METRIC: M3, G2, M1, publisher uplink and CPU, layer-switch latency.
GATE: S3 density gate passes with 5 rooms; publisher uplink increase <= 20 percent; layer-switch visible delay <= ~300 ms.
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_LAYERS=off|2.
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S3 --compare=<previous>; a publisher-side CPU/uplink measurement on a mid-range laptop; a recorded focus-switch to eyeball the layer pop.
acceptance_criteria:
- A written measurement of the publisher, SFU, viewer and compositor consequences before the change ships.
- Two layers only, chosen from t20 numbers.
- Layer pinned from tile geometry and re-pinned on layout change, with the promotion delay measured.
- S3 density gate passes, or the bead is closed with numbers explaining why simulcast was rejected.

title: Ingest discipline: cap publisher resolution and bitrate for what tiles actually need
description:
The studio captures at ideal 1920x1080@30 and publishes with maxBitrate 10 Mbps (STREAM_PROFILES.ingestVideoBps). A grid tile is ~380x216 and even a focus tile is 1920x1080, so 10 Mbps is far above what YouTube will ever see after our 6 Mbps encode, and every extra pixel is decoded 5 rooms x 10 streams times on one T4.

The density reason this matters: 5 rooms x 10 on-scene streams = 50 concurrent H.264 decodes on a single Turing NVDEC, whose real-time budget is roughly 35-40 streams at 1080p30 and about double that at 720p30. So decode saturates before the CPU does unless the ingest resolution comes down or the tiles get their own layers (t22).

Changes, chosen by measurement rather than taste:
- Default camera ingest 1280x720@30 with maxBitrate ~2.5-4 Mbps (YouTube guidance for 720p30 is 1.5-4 Mbps; our output is 1080p30 at 6 Mbps, so a 720p source upscaled in the compositor is inside the quality envelope for a talking-head show).
- Screen share keeps a higher resolution (detail matters more than motion): 1080p or native, contentHint detail, lower fps (5-15) and a higher bitrate ceiling.
- Optional refinement, only if the bench says the focus tile suffers: raise the featured peer to 1080p30 with track.applyConstraints when they become featured, and drop them back when they leave focus. Measure the switch latency and whether viewers see a quality pop.
- Update STREAM_PROFILES.ingestVideoBps and the getUserMedia constraints in web/src/hooks/useStudioSession.ts together so they cannot drift.

This bead changes what speakers publish, so it needs an explicit owner decision on the focus-tile quality trade-off.
design:
SCENARIO: S2, S3.
METRIC: M3, G2 gpu.dec_pct at 5 rooms, focus-tile quality (subjective + a still-frame comparison), publisher uplink.
GATE: M3 down in proportion to the pixel reduction; G2 at 5 rooms below ~70 percent of the NVDEC budget; Q7 still passes on the program output; owner accepts the focus quality.
TOGGLE: COMPOSITOR_INGEST_CAP=720p30|1080p30|native (drives the bench publisher constraints too, so both sides move together).
PROOF: npm run bench -- --scenario=S3 --compare=<previous> on the box with nvidia-smi dmon -s u running; still-frame capture of a focus tile at each setting.
acceptance_criteria:
- Camera and screen-share ingest constraints are decided from measurements and documented.
- 50 concurrent decodes stay inside the NVDEC budget at 5 rooms (G2 recorded).
- Program output still passes Q7; focus-tile stills compared and approved by the owner.
- Profile and getUserMedia constraints updated together with a test that they agree.

title: Pin the ffmpeg build instead of pulling BtbN latest
description:
compositor/Dockerfile curls https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases/download/latest/ffmpeg-master-latest-linux64-gpl.tar.xz. That floating tag is what broke NVENC on the box: driver 595.91.07 exposes NVENC API 13.0 and the latest build was compiled against 13.1, so h264_nvenc listed itself in -encoders but failed to open, and every session silently downgraded to software MediaRecorder encode (commit 20c0657 documents this).

Changes:
- Pin a specific BtbN release tag (or a specific ffmpeg version) and verify the tarball sha256 in the Dockerfile.
- Keep the build-time grep for h264_nvenc, and add the ffmpeg version to the boot log and to /internal/health so a mismatch is visible without SSH.
- If t5 outcome A removes NVENC from the media path, ffmpeg is still needed for muxing, tee and the Opus->AAC transcode, so the pin still matters - just retitle the acceptance around determinism rather than NVENC.
- Note in the README why the pin exists (a floating build tag is a production incident waiting to happen).
design:
SCENARIO: none (build determinism).
METRIC: ffmpeg version and NVENC API version reported at boot.
GATE: two rebuilds a week apart produce the identical ffmpeg version string; the boot log and /internal/health show it.
TOGGLE: n/a.
PROOF: docker compose build compositor twice; compare ffmpeg -version output from the image.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dockerfile references a pinned release with a checksum.
- Boot log and /internal/health expose the ffmpeg version.
- README explains the pin.

title: Cleanup: remove A/B toggles, final before/after report, persist the findings
description:
Close the epic properly.

- Remove the experimental toggles introduced along the way (COMPOSITOR_FPS stays as a documented setting; COMPOSITOR_CAPTURE, COMPOSITOR_REDRAW, COMPOSITOR_LOOP, COMPOSITOR_CANVAS, COMPOSITOR_CANVAS_DESYNC, COMPOSITOR_TEXT_CACHE, COMPOSITOR_LAYOUT_MEMO, COMPOSITOR_AUDIO, COMPOSITOR_ENCODE, COMPOSITOR_SCENE_FILTER, COMPOSITOR_INGEST_CAP, COMPOSITOR_HW_DECODE, COMPOSITOR_LAYERS, COMPOSITOR_ENCODE_PROBE) and the losing code paths behind them. Keep only the documented production settings plus COMPOSITOR_ALLOW_SOFTWARE_ENCODE for dev.
- Run the full scenario set one last time and attach the final before/after table to the epic: baseline (t3) versus final, for M1-M4, Q1-Q7, C1-C3, G1-G3, wire rate, rooms per box.
- bd remember the durable findings so the next session does not rediscover them: ANGLE gl-egl is the only Linux backend that composites on hardware; Chromium has no NVENC backend so VAAPI + nvidia-vaapi-driver is the only hardware video path on NVIDIA Linux; the exact LIBVA/NVD env and feature flags that worked; the muxer choice and why; the YouTube output settings; the NVDEC density math (roughly 35-40 concurrent 1080p30 streams on a T4); never feed ffmpeg a fixed -r for a source that can drop frames.
- Close the epic when its acceptance criteria are all met.
design:
SCENARIO: S1, S2, S4, S5 (final numbers), S3 on the box.
METRIC: all.
GATE: no experimental toggle remains except the documented ones; the final report is attached; every acceptance item on the epic is checked.
PROOF: grep for COMPOSITOR_ in the repo and compare with the documented list; npm run bench -- --scenario=S2 --compare=bench/out/baseline-S2.json.
acceptance_criteria:
- Experimental toggles and losing code paths removed; documented settings only.
- Final before/after report attached to the epic.
- Durable findings saved with bd remember.
- typecheck, tests, lint and CI green; the epic acceptance criteria are all met and the epic is closed.
